design:
Tier 2 (permission posture). No migration; runners already storing an override flag are refused at launch (D2), not rewritten. Rollback: revert.
D1. One rule, `runner_flag_rules.posture_flags_problem(cli, flags)`, used by create, PATCH and the probe, so the three cannot disagree.
D2. Stored flags are judged in `probe_agent` (the launchability verdict the trigger already gates on, `agent_wide`, input kept), not silently stripped: stripping would run the runner differently from what it says it is.
D3. Copilot keeps its run-time stripping of widening flags (they are legitimate under Full access); only --model is refused for it.
D4. F469 (show flags read-only on the Runners page) is UI work and stays its own item.

checked: runner_commands.py:296 appends extra_flags after the Hub's flags
runner_provider.py:73 refuses --model only on provider runners
Drive on :8031: seven override runners accepted; Add-agent bound the flagged runner
limits: Codex is not drivable here; its rules are unit-tested only

problem: `runner_commands._build_claude_command` appends `extra_flags` after the Hub's own `--model` and `--permission-mode` (`runner_commands.py:296`), so a runner created with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--model` overrides both: in the 2026-10-15 sweep such a runner's turn wrote outside the workspace while the roster said `workspace`. `provider_flags_problem` refuses `--model` on provider runners only (`runner_provider.py:73`). Add-agent's find-or-create (`agents.py:734`) selects any runner with the same cli and model, unordered, flags and provider config ignored, and bound the flagged one.

requirements.rationale: The posture is the operator's safety control and the model their spend; a free-form flag must not silently override either.
requirements.statement: POST and PATCH /runners MUST refuse flags that set the model or the permission posture for the runner's CLI -- Claude: --model, --permission-mode, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --allowedTools/--allowed-tools, --disallowedTools/--disallowed-tools, --permission-prompt-tool, --add-dir, --settings; Codex: --model/-m, --sandbox/-s, --ask-for-approval/-a, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, --full-auto, --add-dir, and -c/--config setting model, sandbox or approval keys; Copilot: --model -- in both `--flag value` and `--flag=value` form, naming the field or setting that owns each.

requirements.rationale: Runners created before this change exist on live databases.
requirements.statement: A runner whose stored flags hold one of them MUST be reported not launchable, naming the flag and the remedy (PATCH its flags, or delete it), and no turn MAY start on it; the input waits for the repair.

requirements.rationale: The dialog promises 'the Hub provisions the runner for you' from a provider and a model.
requirements.statement: Add-agent by provider and model MUST bind only a runner with that cli and model and no flags and no provider config, the oldest first, and create one when none exists.
Every other flag is accepted and run as today (for example --mcp-config, F531; Copilot's widening flags, which the posture strips at run time).

summary: A runner's flags may not carry the flags that set the model or the permission posture: refused on create and PATCH naming the field that owns them, and a runner that already stores one is not launchable until it is fixed. Add-agent's find-or-create binds only a plain runner (F599, F600).
